transcript:
Header: 2025-02-26 15:00 UTC | Duration 45m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samira Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Marco Ruiz (Apollo DX Head of ML), Linda Chen (Apollo DX Platform Eng), Owen Park (Apollo DX CTO)

Summary: quick QBR to review last quarter's usage/costs, reliability incidents, and next steps toward a private/dedicated evaluation.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hi everyone thanks for joining, I think we've got a full house, should we kick off with a quick agenda?
[00:08] Marco Ruiz: yeah that sounds good, we wanna make sure we cover cost stuff early, that's kind of top of mind for the execs.
[00:13] Priya Nair: to set context, i'll run through the usage / reliability highlights, then Jordan will cover costs and contract stuff, and we can deep dive on networking and SOC2 after that. sound ok?
[00:21] Owen Park: yep, that's good.

[02:05] Priya Nair: ok so on usage — Apollo DX has increased calls by roughly 28% month over month for the last quarter, bursty traffic in late Jan was the highest peak, latencies held up for the most part but we saw two infra blips on Jan 18th and Jan 29th where requests timed out for about 30 seconds in a narrow set of shards. those were traced to autoscaler jitter plus an upstream GC on the customer's service, so a bit of a combined effect.
[02:42] Linda Chen: can you, can you run that back, autoscaler jitter? we thought the Dedicated pool would smooth that out, is that expected?
[02:50] Priya Nair: good question — the blip happened on our hosted infra; on Dedicated we provide pinned capacity so you'd be more protected. the jitter was an internal scaler backoff that we patched Jan 20th; after the patch we didn't see recurrence. some of the timeouts were also impacted by a large batch of requests hitting your side service which exacerbated the tail.
[03:11] Marco Ruiz: ok. so that means if we moved to dedicated, we should expect fewer of these events, yes?
[03:15] Priya Nair: generally yes — Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor effects and gives you predictable throughput. there are tradeoffs on cost, which Jordan will go into next.

[05:02] Jordan Lee: on cost: we've broken down token spend by route and model. your top three routes are: chat-ingest (45%), embedding-index (30%), and rerank (12%). biggest suggestions: enable prefix KV cache for chat-ingest where you have repeated system prompts, and consider quantized variant of the r2-small model for reranking — should reduce per-token cost by ~22% without major quality loss in your evals. also batching windows can be widened during non-peak hours.
[05:27] Linda Chen: when you say quantized variant — what's the compatibility work on our side? we run inference from a VPC, some of our infra folks worry about format changes.
[05:34] Priya Nair: it's transparent on the API side — it's a model variant on our catalog. for Private deployments there's a small extra step for the runtime image since quantization requires specific kernels; our SEs help with that.
[06:00] Owen Park: cost numbers look promising. can you send exact numbers for the last 90 days? execs want a line item view.
[06:06] Jordan Lee: absolutely, i'll send a token-level spreadsheet, with route breakdowns and suggested savings. expect that by next monday.

[08:10] Marco Ruiz: on reliability — aside from the January blips, our SLOs have mostly been met. the big question for us is SLAs for dedicated / private if we move forward in Q2. what's typical SLA for Dedicated?
[08:25] Priya Nair: Dedicated has uptime SLAs in contract — commonly 99.9% plus performance targets, and you can add incident response times as part of an enterprise package. for Private on-prem, SLA depends on customer-managed infra; we offer support SLAs and runbooks.
[08:45] Marco Ruiz: and audit logs and retention? we need 12 months for certain compliance flows.
[08:51] Samira Ortiz: we can configure audit log retention and integrate with your SIEM; for Private deployments logs stay in your environment so retention is under your control. for hosted we have configurable windows and can export logs to your S3.

[11:33] Linda Chen: i'd like to review the SOC2 doc and the network diagram for VPC peering. that'll help our security folks greenlight the pilot.
[11:40] Jordan Lee: yep we'll share SOC2 + infra diagram, i'll have Priya attach the VPC peering checklist.
[11:46] Priya Nair: one note on KMS — for Private we plug into your KMS/HSM; for Hosted we can integrate customer-managed keys for encryption-at-rest. i'll include the steps.

[14:55] Owen Park: timeline question — if we wanted to pilot Dedicated in Q2, what's the on-ramp look like? how long for provisioning and performance validation?
[15:04] Priya Nair: provisioning Dedicated capacity typically takes 2-4 weeks depending on region and GPU type; staging benchmark and validation usually another 1-2 weeks. if we start the procurement and sizing now we can aim for mid-late April pilot.
[15:20] Jordan Lee: and contract negotiations for reserved capacity can go parallel with technical onboarding.

[18:12] Marco Ruiz: for the benchmarking, we want to validate 95th percentile latency under peak traffic and also measure token-cost at different batch sizes. can Redwood run a staging benchmark or provide a harness we can run?
[18:23] Priya Nair: we can run the benchmark SE-led in staging and also share a harness if you prefer to run it internally. for the SE-run benchmarks we'll need your representative prompt set and peak traffic profile.
[18:35] Linda Chen: we'll pull that together. expect the prompt set and traffic profile by Mar 5th.

[21:00] Samira Ortiz: quick note on roadmap: we are planning a managed quantization offering and auto batching recommendations in the console, ETA Q3. those will probably directly address the cost asks you have.
[21:13] Marco Ruiz: awesome. will those be configurable per-route?
[21:18] Samira Ortiz: yes, per-route controls, and we'll provide simulated impact in the console before you flip them on.

[24:40] Jordan Lee: any competitor concerns or procurement nuances?
[24:44] Marco Ruiz: our procurement team is also talking to Anthropic and separately looking at a managed OpenAI contract, mostly for redundancy. cost and data residency are the deciding factors.
[24:56] Owen Park: procurement asked if there's an easy way to fall back to a lower-cost variant during spikes; is routing by policy possible today?
[25:05] Priya Nair: yes — routing by policy exists. you can set latency-first or cost-first policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. we'll show you the policy UI in the console.

[28:10] Linda Chen: on security — two asks: can Redwood provide proof of vulnerability scanning for runtime images and confirm SOC2 section on encryption?
[28:19] Priya Nair: yes on both — we'll attach the vulnerability scan summary and the SOC2 report redacted; encryption-at-rest and in-transit are covered, and we'll include the KMS integration steps.

[31:00] Marco Ruiz: ok let's recap next steps. Jordan will send the usage/cost spreadsheet and recommendations; Priya will send SOC2 + infra docs and coordinate the benchmark; Linda will send the prompt set and traffic profile; Samira will set up the monthly health report cadence.
[31:26] Jordan Lee: correct, and we'll target the staging benchmark for 2025-03-10 pending receipt of the prompts/traffic.

[33:44] Owen Park: any other blockers from Redwood side for a Q2 pilot?
[33:50] Priya Nair: nothing technical we can't handle, just need final alignment on GPU type and sizing; procurement lead time is usually the gating factor.

[36:12] Marco Ruiz: procurement will need pricing line items, can you add a reserved capacity scenario?
[36:19] Jordan Lee: yes i'll include a reserved capacity (3/6/12 month) cost model in the spreadsheet.

[38:40] Linda Chen: last quick question — how often will the model catalog change and how will version pinning work? we want to avoid surprise regressions.
[38:51] Priya Nair: models are added and updated; you can pin model versions per-route and we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback. we'll include a doc on model governance.

[41:00] Marco Ruiz: perfect. thanks everyone, appreciate the concrete next steps.
[41:05] Jordan Lee: thanks all, we'll send items over. we'll follow up in email with attachments and calendar invites for the benchmark.
[41:12] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attributions and small filler words retained; sounding natural and not heavily cleaned up. references to internal Redwood features (kv cache, Dedicated, Private) occasionally shorthand or slightly off-cased (e.g., 'KV cache' vs 'kv cache').
